title: Navigating the base excision repair pathway in chromatin-focus on oxidative DNA damage.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Retrieved the open-access full text (97,665 characters) from Europe PMC and read its data availability statement, which says verbatim 'No new data were generated in this article.' Listed the entire supplementary package (0.61 MB zip): it contains 12 files, all of them figure images (six .webp and six .gif renderings of Figures 1-5 and the graphical abstract) and no tabular file. Searched the whole text for accessions, repository links (GEO/SRA/Zenodo/Dryad/GitHub) and dataset mentions: the only identifiers found are DOIs of cited papers. Printed the full contents of the single table, Table 1, which is a five-row prose comparison of transcription-coupled nucleotide excision repair versus transcription-coupled base excision repair (entries such as 'RNAPII stalling at bulky DNA lesions'), i.e. narrative text, not measurements.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Nothing material; there were no data files to open because none exist. The biology described (base excision repair in chromatin, 8-oxo-dG as both lesion and regulatory signal) is taken from the review's prose and the papers it cites.

a1_downloadable.note: FAIL. This is a review (Survey and Summary) article by Caron, Hans and Timmins; its data availability statement states 'No new data were generated in this article.' The only downloadable attachments are 12 figure image files (.webp/.gif, 0.61 MB total). There is no accession, no repository deposit and no supplementary table anywhere in the text, so there is nothing to download and model.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Not reached in substance: with no file there is no column. Any label (for example, how fast a given oxidised base is excised, or where 8-oxo-dG accumulates) would have to be assembled by hand from the ~200 cited primary papers, which is exactly the 'label must be constructed' failure A2 describes.

a3_inputs_present.note: No input features of any kind are distributed; the article contains prose, five schematic figures and one prose table.

a4_units_stated.note: No numeric quantity with units is distributed in any file.

a5_enough_rows.note: The only table (Table 1) has 5 rows and 3 text columns, far below the ~400-1,500 row floor, and the rows are qualitative statements rather than measurements.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially fits, but only because there is no data.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: No counts to compare; the paper reports no dataset size.

a8_label_provenance.note: No label exists. Labels drawn from a review's text would be the authors' interpretive summary of other groups' experiments, one step removed from any physical measurement.

backbone.licence: CC BY-NC 4.0 (article text and figures only; non-commercial)

honest_claim_h3: No claim is possible from this article: it distributes no measurements, only a narrative synthesis of other laboratories' published work.

plain_idea.one_liner: Considered: use local chromatin state to predict where oxidative DNA damage is repaired fastest across the genome.
plain_idea.train_on: Would need genome-wide maps of chromatin features (histone marks, nucleosome positions, accessibility, transcription level) in fixed windows; this review supplies none of them, so the example count is zero.
plain_idea.predict: Would predict a repair-rate or damage-level readout per genomic window, measured by sequencing assays for oxidised bases such as 8-oxo-dG or abasic sites; those measurements live in other papers' GEO deposits, not here.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Chromatin researchers and cancer-mutagenesis groups would like to know which parts of the genome are protected from oxidative damage, but answering it needs the primary damage-mapping datasets, which this review only cites.

ml_idea: None available from this article. The nearest viable project would start instead from the primary damage-mapping datasets this review cites (for example OG-Seq, Click-code-Seq, snAP-seq and Repair-seq style deposits in GEO), joined to ENCODE chromatin tracks on genomic coordinates; that is a different paper's data and would need its own evaluation.

effort.compute_note: Only 0.61 MB of figure images exists; no compute estimate is meaningful because there is no feature/label table to build.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Done in one step: read the data availability statement ('No new data were generated in this article') and list the supplement (12 figure images, no tables). That kills it immediately.

verdict_reason: Narrative review of base excision repair in chromatin; it explicitly generated no new data, has no accessions or repository deposits, and its supplement is 12 figure images, so A1 fails.
